title: Nociceptors and the microbiota
objective: Explain evidence that gut nociceptors regulate the microbiota and tissue protection.

steps.title: Neurons that tend the garden
steps.body: Gut **[[nociceptor|nociceptors]]** do more than report trouble — they help regulate the **microbiota** and defend the mucosa. Zhang et al. found that gut-innervating nociceptors shape the microbial community in ways that protect the tissue.

steps.setup: You ablate the gut-innervating nociceptors in a mouse and then examine its gut microbiota and mucosal defense.
options: The microbial community and tissue protection shift, often for the worse
The microbiota shifts, but mucosal protection stays exactly the same
Nothing at all changes in the gut after their removal
Only the brain is affected by this, and never the gut
steps.reveal: Removing the neurons changed the microbiota and reduced protection — evidence that nociceptors actively regulate the gut ecosystem, not just sense it. A striking efferent role for 'sensory' neurons.

variants.prompt: Ablating gut nociceptors (which help regulate the microbiota) tends to…
options: Shift the microbiota and weaken the tissue's protection
Leave the gut completely unchanged in every way
Regrow all of the lost neurons almost instantly
variants.explanation: These neurons regulate the microbiota, so removing them alters it and protection.

steps.prompt: What broader idea does nociceptor control of the microbiota support?
options: The nervous system is an active regulator of host–microbe balance
Neurons and microbes never influence one another in any way
Only antibodies, never neurons, can shape the microbiota
The microbiota is completely fixed and cannot be regulated
steps.explanation: It places neurons among the regulators of the microbiome — extending neuroimmunology to the host–microbe interface.

variants.setup: Nociceptors can shape which microbes thrive in the gut.
variants.reveal: Neurons are active regulators of the host–microbe relationship.

sources.note: Gut-innervating nociceptors regulate the microbiota to promote tissue protection.
